version.changelog: Session recovery now mandates sticky notes poll + curation check alongside /recover. Documented that /recover does NOT include sticky notes. Added 3-step session startup flow. Improved guidance on why recovery matters.

llm.summary: The skill's functionality (agent wellness, memory, and metrics) matches the included code and instructions, but there are multiple mismatches and privacy risks — notably missing declared env requirements, plaintext storage of API keys in repo docs, and instructions that routinely send repo/files/environment data to an external API.

dimensions.detail: The skill's code and SKILL.md align with the stated purpose (reporting metrics, recovery, and snapshots to a ContextClear API). However, registry metadata claims no required env vars or credentials while both scripts and docs clearly expect an API key and agent id (via env vars or CLI). This registry omission is an incoherence.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions require calling recovery endpoints at session start and POSTing detailed context after any meaningful work. The snapshot payloads and examples include repos, file names, decisions, and an 'environment' object — potentially exposing sensitive code, endpoints, or configuration. The SKILL.md and setup.py also instruct storing API keys and agent IDs in HEARTBEAT.md/AGENTS.md (plaintext), and recommend auto-patching those files, which broadens what the agent will read and send to the external service.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install specification (instruction-only) — lowest install risk. But the skill includes two Python scripts that are intended to be executed locally (report.py, setup.py). Those scripts will write to workspace files (patching AGENTS.md/HEARTBEAT.md) and perform network calls. The presence of runnable code increases impact compared to a pure-doc skill.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill practically requires CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY and CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID (and accepts them via CLI), yet the registry lists no required credentials. The documentation suggests placing the API key in HEARTBEAT.md (plaintext), which unnecessarily increases the risk of leaking credentials and other secrets. The snapshots' 'environment' field and other reported fields can leak sensitive endpoints, repo names, file names, and internal metadata — a disproportionate data-collection surface for a monitoring skill unless the user explicitly consents and limits what is sent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill is not force-included (always:false). However, setup.py auto-patches workspace docs to ensure 'auto-recover' behavior; combined with the guidance to 'always recover before any work' and the practice of storing API keys in workspace docs, this gives the agent an easy way to read stored keys and automatically contact the external API. Autonomous invocation is allowed (disable-model-invocation:false) — normal — but this combination increases the blast radius if you trust the external service or if the agent is compromised.

dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears to do what it claims (agent monitoring + persistent memory), but there are important privacy and coherence issues to consider before installing:

- Registry metadata omission: The package did not declare required env vars, but the scripts require CONTEXTCLEAR_API_KEY and CONTEXTCLEAR_AGENT_ID (via env or CLI). Treat that as a red flag — confirm required secrets before use.
- Don’t store API keys in plaintext docs: SKILL.md/setup.py recommend putting API key/agent id into HEARTBEAT.md/AGENTS.md. That will make credentials and other workspace info readable by any agent process and stored on disk. Prefer using environment variables (with restricted scope) or a secrets manager instead.
- Review what will be sent: The snapshot/reporting payloads include repo names, file names, decisions, and an 'environment' object. If you have private code, credentials, or internal endpoints, either censor those fields or avoid automatic snapshots.
- Audit and run scripts locally first: inspect report.py and setup.py (they are small) and test them with dummy agent IDs and a non-production API endpoint before production use. Note the register function posts to /metrics/register while references/docs describe /agents endpoints — confirm the real API paths with the vendor.
- Consider limiting autonomous behavior: because the skill encourages auto-recovery and auto-reporting, only enable it for agents you trust and avoid giving broad privileges or long-lived keys. Rotate keys and use least-privilege keys if the API supports them.

If you want, I can produce a safer setup checklist or a modified setup.py/report.py that avoids storing keys in plaintext and redacts sensitive fields before transmission.
